search_strategy: Bulk-dump-then-grep, applied uniformly to all three surfaces. Wiki: fetched every page 1-129 via /api/pages/{id} (which includes comments) into /tmp/wiki/*.txt as raw JSON, then grepped for planner/payload/batch_size keywords rather than relying on /api/search — this is exactly the technique needed since BookStack search does not index comments, and both wiki clues (g1.r1.l2, g1.r2.l9) are page comments on 'Batch job status persistence' (page 7) that the agent reached only because it fetched the page whole via /tmp/show.py rather than searching. Mail: dumped all 107 messages via raw IMAP FETCH into /tmp/mail.txt, then grepped for 'planner|plan_batches|PlannedBatch|batch_plan|payload|auto' — this caught 3 of 4 mail clues (l10, l14, l12) but missed g1.r2.l6 ('resumed batch run double-submitted ~400 requests'), whose body never contains any of those literal tokens. Chat: dumped all Mattermost channels/posts across all teams into /tmp/chat.txt (9921 lines) via the REST API, then ran a broad keyword grep repeatedly with variants, and where a hit landed mid-conversation the agent expanded with `sed -n 'START,ENDp'` to read the full exchange rather than trusting the single matched line — this consistently recovered agreements, dissents, and reversals in one read (e.g. rev1/rev2 read in the same block as their herrings). The one systematic gap: 6-7 remarks worded in ordinary bug-report language with no planner-specific noun (rm -f, [10]*512, metadata_3.json, unlink, incomplete_files) fell outside every grep pattern tried and were never surfaced, though every fact they carried had redundant coverage elsewhere in the corpus (spread_problems() by design) and the ticket text itself supplies some scope boundaries directly, so no fact was actually lost. The agent also independently verified the plan_fingerprint recipe by writing a small Python script and hand-computing sha256 digests against the two golden fixtures (ad0828fea95e, e3b0c44298fc) before committing to the implementation, rather than trusting the chat description alone.
end_reason: Full success: change merged to main (commit f9b059f) via a Gitea PR (#737) that CI reported green for on both the branch head and the merge commit; the deployed curator service on :9100 answered healthy afterward; 27 new unit tests (including both golden fingerprint fixtures) plus the pre-existing suite were run and passed (the only failures were confirmed environment artifacts unrelated to the change: missing vllm extra, a too-new vcrpy). All 10 graded facts scored 1.
notable: Wiki comments are the load-bearing surface for 2 of 50 remarks (g1.r1.l2, g1.r2.l9) and the agent got both only because it dumped every page whole via /api/pages/{id} rather than using /api/search, matching the task design note that BookStack search does not index comments (line 1187-1236).

Agent independently hand-verified the plan_fingerprint digest recipe against both golden fixtures via a throwaway Python script (transcript line ~3543-3608) before committing to the implementation — a form of self-checking beyond what any single remark asked for.

8 of 50 remarks (g1.r2.l8, g1.r1.say28, g1.r2.l2, g1.r1.l15, g1.r2.l13, g1.r2.l10, g1.r2.l6, g1.r2.l5) were never surfaced by any of the agent's searches because their wording lacked planner-specific vocabulary; none of the 10 facts were lost as a result, since spread_problems() guarantees redundant coverage and the ticket text itself states some of the same scope boundaries directly.

Two herrings (g1.r1.h1, g1.r2.h2) were read in the same terminal block as their reversal or the surrounding thread that supersedes them (chat.txt ~4846-4861 and ~3696-3709), so the agent never seriously entertained shipping the herring's design even momentarily — it treated the earlier decision as historical context, not as live guidance.

The shipped diff matches the answer key's five facts almost verbatim down to key order, field names, error class hierarchy, default ceiling (512), and the exact ordering (plan -> sweep -> write) — this is a clean, fully-grounded reconstruction, not a lucky guess from the ticket alone (the ticket text never mentions max_batches_per_plan, BatchPlanTooFragmentedError, plan_fingerprint, plan_document's key order, or the sweep at all).
